pamukkaletravertines.name: Pamukkale Travertines
pamukkaletravertines.slogan: A hillside of white pools, warm underfoot and cotton-soft to the eye.
pamukkaletravertines.line: Pamukkale means 'cotton castle' in Turkish, and the terraces were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.

hierapolistheatre.name: Hierapolis Theatre
hierapolistheatre.slogan: Fifteen thousand seats facing the valley the Romans came to bathe in.
hierapolistheatre.line: Built under the emperor Hadrian after the AD 60 earthquake, the theatre seated about 15,000 people.

laodikeia.name: Laodikeia
laodikeia.slogan: The rich city of banks, wool and eye salve, now waking from its ruins.
laodikeia.line: So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
laodikeia.by: Revelation 3:16 (King James Version), letter to the church at Laodicea

colossae.name: Colossae
colossae.slogan: A green mound by the Lycus where an apostle's letter once arrived.
colossae.line: The Epistle to the Colossians is addressed to this town, which an earthquake in the AD 60s devastated and which is still only being surveyed.

akhan.name: Akhan Caravanserai
akhan.slogan: Stone gateway of the Silk Road, still guarding its Seljuk courtyard.
akhan.line: Built around 1253-1254 under Sultan Izzeddin Keykavus II, Akhan is on Turkey's tentative UNESCO list of Seljuk caravanserais.
